paragraphs.text: This variety of visions shows the great unbelief of the people, whose captivity and calamity is here further described and assured by a new type, which is set out in Eze 12:1-6:, and then applied in Eze 12:7-16. One sermon pegs in another, and the man of God must stick to his work, and επιστηθι, stand over it. {2Ti 4:2}
paragraphs.anchor: The word of the Lord also came unto me.

paragraphs.text: Heb., A house of rebellion, domus perduellis, that hath cast down the gauntlet of defiance against me.
paragraphs.anchor: A rebellious house.

paragraphs.text: sc., To any good purpose. They will not see, {Isa 26:11} and who so blind as such? They wink wilfully, which is no small aggravation of their sin. {Joh 9:4 Eph 4:18}
paragraphs.anchor: Which have eyes to see, and see not

paragraphs.text: i.e., Castigatiores non evadunt. They are not a button the better for what they hear. They draw not up the ears of their minds to the ears of their bodies, that one sound might pierce both.
paragraphs.anchor: Which have ears to hear, and hear not

paragraphs.text: i.e., Nevertheless do thou as thou art bidden, and let what thou doest and sayest be for a testimony against them, stick in their souls and flesh, as the envenomed arrows of the Almighty throughout eternity.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore, thou son of man

paragraphs.text: Heb., Instruments, or vessels. Convasa res tuas, collae sarcinas, pack up and away. See if this way thou canst work upon them.
paragraphs.anchor: Prepare thee stuff for removing.

paragraphs.text: sc., By this express sign, though they profit not by thy plain preaching. Ministers must study their people’s souls; turn themselves into all forms and shapes, of spirit and of speech, to win upon them.
paragraphs.anchor: It may be they will consider

paragraphs.text: Arma viatoria; travelling bags for an ocular demonstration. What surer than sight?
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt bring forth thy stuff.

paragraphs.text: The king and his men of war were glad to do so, {2Ki 25:4} but it would not do.
paragraphs.anchor: Go forth at even.

paragraphs.text: Make any shift. Necessitas magnum telum. He that digged Mortimer’s hole, as they call it, at Nottingham Castle, earned his liberty dearly. God might have said to the prophet at once, Get thee gone out of thy country - how sad a thing that is Ovid when banished setteth forth in many elegant elegies, sed cuncta per partes digerit - but he must do it piecemeal and by degrees, that it may the more affect them.
paragraphs.anchor: Dig through the wall.

paragraphs.text: To show that King Zedekiah himself should carry out some of his most precious things upon his shoulders when he fled. See Eze 12:12. This was a base thing for a king to do. King Alphonsus indeed is renowned for drawing a poor perishing man out of a ditch, and bearing him on his back to a place of relief.
paragraphs.anchor: In their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders.

paragraphs.text: In token that Zedekiah should be made blind. A just hand of God upon him who had eyes and saw not, {Eze 12:2} like as it was upon Muleasses King of Tunis, who had those eyes of his dug out which had been inlets of lust, and which he oft covered with his hat pulled over them, that he might listen the better to wanton ditties and profane music.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt cover thy face.

paragraphs.text: Portentum, a sign portending their going into captivity.
paragraphs.anchor: For I have set thee for a sign.

paragraphs.text: And [did as I was commanded.] Though well laughed at for my labour by the mad world, ever beside itself in point of salvation, and looking upon God’s Jordans as Naaman did, with Syrian eyes. The outward signs in our sacraments are in themselves mean and ordinary matters; yet the minister is to make use of them, and the people to climb up to heaven by them as ladders of life Hence even in the ancient church liturgy they had their Sursum corda, Lift up your hearts. Rideant athei et ringantur.
Mane, id est, mature. God not only betime, but timeously, admonished his people; but they refused to be reformed - would have none of his counsel.
paragraphs.anchor: And in the morning came the word of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Hath not the house of Israel … said unto thee, What doest thou?] {a} q.d., Nothing less. So stupid they are, or so stubborn, that they never once asked any such question; or if they did, it was in a jeer, as who should say, You are a wise man to trouble yourself and us in this foolish and childish manner; a great deal of gravity sure you show therewhile.
{a} Quid sibi vult quod ita migras? Tu, habet emphasin. - Lavat.
There is an elegance in the original. Princes who overburden their people shall one day have their back burden of miseries. Potentes potenter torquebuntur.
paragraphs.anchor: This burden concerneth the princes in Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: And so it pleases you to make me your mocking stock. Sed risus hic est Sardonius. Of such mirth one may safely say, "It is mad; and of such laughter, What doeth it?" {Ecc 2:2}
paragraphs.anchor: I am your sign.

paragraphs.text: My removal is mira, nova inimica, et ludicra; a marvel, newly hostile, and a show; but upon you it will fall heavily and horridly. That which hath befallen me in type only, shall befall you in truth and reality.
paragraphs.anchor: Like as I have done.

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah, that profane, wicked prince. {Eze 21:25}
paragraphs.anchor: And the prince that is among them.

paragraphs.text: His precious things (see on Eze 12:6). This, though it be not recorded in the holy history, yet that it was so, we are assured by this scripture. Great men in exigents stoop to low offices. This load upon his shoulders might hinder his flight and further his surprise, as it did Bajazet’s, when he was beaten out of the field by Tamerlane, that he stayed to water his horse. The Vulgate rendereth it, but not well, in humeris portabitur, he shall be carried on men’s shoulders. The Pope, indeed, is ordinarily so carried; but he was glad to foot it when forced by the German and Spanish soldiers; A.D. 1527, he was glad to secure himself in his castle St Angelo.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall bear upon his shoulders in the twilight.

paragraphs.text: The door haply, or inlet of some underground passage.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall dig through the wall.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 12:6. This he did haply through fear, or shame, or for a disguise; but his sin found him out.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall cover his face.

paragraphs.text: Princes usually love hunting and fowling. Lo, the Chaldees shall hunt him and overcatch him.
paragraphs.anchor: My net also will I spread upon him.

paragraphs.text: Snares are set secretly, catch suddenly, hold certainly. A stronghold the Hebrew word here used doth also signify. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And he shall be taken in my snare.

paragraphs.text: For his eyes were put out at Riblah. {2Ki 25:7} And yet, behold, a greater blindness that befell him than this. Josephus {b} testifieth that Zedekiah not understanding these words of Ezekiel, and thinking them to be contrary to Jeremiah’s words, he resolved to believe neither of them.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet shall he not see it.

paragraphs.text: {a} Jun.
{b} Joseph. Ant., lib. vi. x., cap. 10.

His bodyguard, σοματοφυλακες. Esquires of his body, auxiliaries. I will put him into a helpless condition. {Psa 146:3} If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? said that king to her that cried to him for help. {2Ki 6:27}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will scatter toward every wind.

paragraphs.text: The Lord God of heaven, the great and terrible God. {Neh 1:5} This they shall know magno suo male, his great wrong, who would not take knowledge what was said unto them by the prophets.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall know that I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Men of number, a company scarce considerable in comparison of the many.
paragraphs.anchor: But I will leave a few men.

paragraphs.text: Give glory to God, take shame to themselves, and thereby do much good to those heathens hardened before by their evil behaviour. Vere magnus est Deus Christianorum, Truly, great is the God of the Christians, said one Calocerius, a heathen.
paragraphs.anchor: That they may declare all their abominations.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 12:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the word, &c.

paragraphs.text: With tumult and trepidation, as a frightened and perplexed person that eateth his bread in peril of his life.
paragraphs.anchor: Eat thy bread with quaking.

paragraphs.text: Better fast than feed on such bread. Men may sooner by their carking care add a furlong to their grief, than a cubit to their comfort, saith one.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall eat their bread with carefulness.

paragraphs.text: The Jews were ever, and are still, a covetous and cruel people.
paragraphs.anchor: Because of the violence.

paragraphs.text: By woeful experience. {Eze 12:15}
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall know.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 12:1.
paragraphs.anchor: And the word of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: We have also many profane proverbs common among us, as, Thought is free; Every man for himself, and God for us all; Words are but wind; In space comes grace; Fair and softly goes far, &c. The Greeks had many such ill proverbs, Chrysostom complaineth.
paragraphs.anchor: What is that proverb.

paragraphs.text: Ludibrium crassum: gross mockery, "Because judgment is not speedily executed," &c.
paragraphs.anchor: The days are prolonged.

paragraphs.text: Opponit aliud dictum fere tot syllabarum; a plain and plenary confutation.
paragraphs.anchor: The days are at hand.

paragraphs.text: God could have really confuted them by present execution; but he is patient.
paragraphs.anchor: For there shall be no more.

paragraphs.text: And that you shall shortly feel to your small comfort. What I have uttered with my mouth, I will perform with my hand without fail.
paragraphs.anchor: For I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Within six years.
paragraphs.anchor: For in your days.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 12:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Again the word.

paragraphs.text: Either it is nothing, or long hence.
paragraphs.anchor: For many days.

paragraphs.text: Abused mercy turneth into fury.
paragraphs.anchor: There shall none of my words be prolonged.
